extractor: read directly from the official GOV.UK pages listed in source_roles
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from. source_excerpt is verbatim government wording, lowercased by the normalizer. Nothing here is paraphrased into a requirement, and nothing is included that the page did not state. The UK publishes no application form identifier for this route, so official_form_code is null everywhere and the online route is recorded as a step.
not_extracted: The registered 'forms' source https://visas-immigration.service.gov.uk/product/uk-visit-visa was NOT fetched. That host's robots.txt is 'User-agent: *' / 'Disallow: /', so the whole site is off limits to the monitor. It is therefore absent from source_roles and no requirement cites it.

Extra eligibility requirements for visiting to study, as an academic, for a permitted paid engagement, or for medical reasons. GOV.UK splits each onto its own sub-page (/visit-to-study, /visit-as-an-academic, /visit-for-a-paid-engagement, /visit-for-medical-reasons) and none of those is a registered source.
Requirements for visitors under 18. They live on the unregistered sub-page /standard-visitor/if-youre-under-18.

The list of nationalities that need a visa, an ETA, or neither. GOV.UK gates it behind the separate 'check if you need a UK visa' tool, so VisaAI cannot yet tell an applicant which of the three applies to them.
The Visitor in Transit visa fee (the apply page mentions GBP 74.50) — that is a different visa product, not a Standard Visitor visa fee, so it is not recorded as a fee on this visa type.
The healthcare surcharge. The Standard Visitor pages do not mention it, and inferring it from another route's page would be inventing a fee.
Priority / faster-decision service fees. The apply page links to 'check to see if you can get your visa decision faster' but states no amount.

requirements.label: Do only the activities permitted for a Standard Visitor
requirements.description: GOV.UK also states that as a Standard Visitor you cannot claim public funds (benefits), cannot live in the UK for long periods through frequent or successive visits, and cannot marry, register a civil partnership or give notice of either — that needs a Marriage Visitor visa.
requirements.source_excerpt: you cannot: do paid or unpaid work for a uk company or as a self-employed person, unless you’re doing a permitted paid engagement or event
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You cannot: do paid or unpaid work for a UK company or as a self-employed person, unless you’re doing a permitted paid engagement or event

requirements.source_excerpt_display: You can usually stay in the UK for up to 6 months. You might be able to apply to stay for longer in certain circumstances, for example to get medical treatment.

requirements.label: Extra details some applicants must give, depending on circumstances
requirements.description: GOV.UK lists these under "depending on your circumstances, you might also need to provide": details of your travel history for the past 10 years; your employer's address and telephone number; your partner's name, date of birth and passport number; the name and address of anyone paying for your trip; the name, address and passport number of any family members you have in the UK. The page states no rule for which of these applies to whom, so VisaAI shows the list rather than guessing.

requirements.label: Apply online before you travel, and book an appointment at a visa application centre
requirements.description: The UK publishes no application form number for this route — the application exists only as an online service. GOV.UK also states you can save the form and finish it later, that each family member needs their own application and fee, and that you can apply on behalf of a partner or child who cannot apply for themselves.
requirements.source_excerpt: if you need a standard visitor visa, you must apply online before you travel to the uk and attend an appointment at a visa application centre. the earliest you can apply is 3 months before you travel.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: If you need a Standard Visitor visa, you must apply online before you travel to the UK and attend an appointment at a visa application centre. The earliest you can apply is 3 months before you travel.

requirements.label: Give the required information in your online application
requirements.description: GOV.UK lists: the dates you're planning to travel to the UK; where you'll be staying during your visit; how much you think your trip will cost; your current home address and how long you've lived there; your parents' names and dates of birth (if known); how much you earn in a year (if you have an income); details of any criminal, civil or immigration offences you may have committed.
requirements.source_excerpt: you’ll need to provide the following information in your online application: the dates you’re planning to travel to the uk
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You’ll need to provide the following information in your online application: the dates you’re planning to travel to the UK

requirements.label: Prove your identity and give biometrics at a visa application centre
requirements.description: GOV.UK notes the visa application centre could be in another country, that your passport is returned the same day, and that the centre may keep some of your other documents while the application is processed.
requirements.source_excerpt: at your appointment, you’ll need to: prove your identity with your passport or travel document ... have your fingerprints and a photo (biometric information) taken ... provide the required documents that show you’re eligible for a standard visitor visa
requirements.source_excerpt_display: At your appointment, you’ll need to: prove your identity with your passport or travel document ... have your fingerprints and a photo (biometric information) taken ... provide the required documents that show you’re eligible for a Standard Visitor visa

requirements.label: Standard Visitor visa application fee
requirements.description: GOV.UK publishes six tiers. The short visit is GBP 135 for up to 6 months; medical-reasons and academic visits cost GBP 234; the long-term visitor visas cost GBP 506 (2 years), GBP 903 (5 years) and GBP 1,128 (10 years), each allowing a maximum stay of 6 months per visit. Each person applying pays their own fee, and there is no refund if a shorter visa is granted or the application is refused.

tiers.tier: standard visitor visa for medical reasons
